record.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark always uses the first host destination, so creation for a cohost credential targets the organizer's calendar instead of that cohost's calendar.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff for LarkCalendarService.ts, the createEvent method at line 128 shows: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`. This destructuring always takes the first element of the destinationCalendar array. Unlike GoogleCalendarService which was updated to accept a credentialId parameter and find the matching calendar (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` where selectedCalendar uses `.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), LarkCalendarService's createEvent signature wasn't updated to accept credentialId. This means for collective team events where multiple destination calendars exist, Lark will always use the first (organizer's) calendar instead of the appropriate cohost's calendar.
